newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria FIS leader gets five years in jail.
newsitem.headline: Algeria FIS leader gets five years in jail.

text.p: Abdelkader Hachani, who headed the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) at the height of its power in 1991, was sentenced to five years in jail for attemtping to undermine state security, the official APS news agency said.
He was also sentenced to three years deprivation of civil rights, APS said, quoting the criminal court of Algiers.
"Abdelkader Hachani, the former leader of banned FIS party, was sentenced on Monday evening to five years imprisonment and three years deprivation of civil rights," APS said.
The prosecutor-general had asked the court to sentence Hachani, who was being tried along with three journalists from Al Khabar newspaper, to 10 years in prison and loss of civil rights.
All were charged with publishing "erroneous and tendentious information likely to harm national interest and national unity." A court spokesman said the Al Khabar journalists were all acquitted.

Hachani was arrested on January 22, 1992 after a statement in his name appeared in Al Khabar paper in the emotionally-charged days after the authorities had cancelled a general election in which the FIS had taken a massive lead. The cancellation sparked violence in which about 60,000 people have died.
